channel.title: VICEPULSE news
channel.description: Takedowns, leaks, legal news, scams and real progress on running GTA VI on PC.

item.title: Belobug’s AMD build renders GTA VI’s open world at 3–5 FPS
item.description: The Radeon fork shows textured streets, traffic, vegetation and water. Driving runs at about 3 FPS on an RX 9070 XT.

item.title: GTA VI PC builds report longer runs at 1–5 FPS
item.description: ZETTROX reports a 90-minute session. A contributor testing the AnyXboxX team’s VIctory fork reports finishing two missions.

item.title: Leonida V2 joins the Watchlist as ZETTROX opens its source
item.description: Leonida V2 reports a blank startup window. ZETTROX has published its code, and PortWatch reports a second build reaching “Gone Fishing.”

item.title: Private GTA VI PC build reportedly reaches Jason’s first mission
item.description: PortWatch VI credits ZETTROX with getting past Lucia’s prologue into “Gone Fishing” at about 2 FPS.

item.title: GitHub processes Take-Two’s takedown across Leonida’s fork network
item.description: GitHub says the notice was processed against a network of 3,007 repositories, including the original.

item.title: GTA VI PC tracker now scores rendering, frame rate and stability
item.description: The new leaderboard separates getting into the game from correct graphics, sustained 30 FPS and crash-free sessions.

item.title: GTA VI footage surfaces on a reported M5 Max MacBook
item.description: A 41-second clip shows GTA VI scenes on a laptop identified by the poster as an M5 Max. Character models and some textures are visible, though lighting and materials still look inconsistent.

item.title: omonkey reportedly reaches GTA VI’s prison scene at about 5 FPS
item.description: PortWatch VI reports character movement and partial shader rendering in a private Windows build. It also reports progress on Five Star Recomp.

item.title: GTA VI PC footage shows sunlight and working lamps
item.description: A new 17-second clip shows bright light on Lucia and visible ceiling lamps, while much of the room stays almost black. The exact build is unconfirmed.

item.title: The next GTA VI PC milestone is a crash-free session
item.description: VICEPULSE is watching for a documented 30-minute gameplay run after a fast jump from menus to the game world.

item.title: Exclusive: CGBJ gets GTA VI in game, walking and talking in an unlit world
item.description: A private build based on VIctory and XCL lets a player walk around and talk to NPCs, very slowly. A video shows the opening scenes in flat colours, without lighting.

item.title: Exclusive: XCL reports 30 fps in GTA VI but won't say if it's past the menus
item.description: The team refused to say more for fear of being nuked, but hinted to one of our members that it's working really well. Update: testers' reports now show it loading into the world.

item.title: TuxBox draws GTA VI's first screen as VIctory edges into the world
item.description: Overnight, a Linux-first layer showed GTA VI's player-selection prompt, VIctory reported a title card inside the game world, and two smaller projects got GTA VI's code running.

item.title: Leonida is nuked: GitHub repo deleted, Discord gone, creator quits
item.description: Within an hour on Monday night the biggest GTA VI port lost its Discord server and its GitHub repository, and its creator said he was stepping away.

item.title: Leonida's Discord server disappears as the project moves to a new GitHub account
item.description: The 179,000-member server stopped resolving late on Monday. Members say Discord banned it; nobody has said why. Update: the GitHub repository has since been deleted too.

item.title: Exclusive: Marvis livestreams GTA VI reaching its menus at about 15 fps
item.description: He has since published the code as VIctory, but nobody else has reproduced the run yet. Viewers who studied the stream think it is most likely real.

item.title: Leonida gets GTA VI's executable running, but nothing is on screen yet
item.description: Contributors' builds run the game's own code for minutes behind a blank window; posts in its Discord say it won't be playable today, but maybe tomorrow.

item.title: Cyberleek's README frames the leak as a protest and asks for crypto
item.description: A note said to ship with the executable says donations fund a secret project and counts every token trade as a vote. None of it can be checked.

item.title: Cyberleek says the missing GTA VI executable is out, hours before its own deadline
item.description: The leaker posted the release at 15:36 CET. Nobody has confirmed the file is genuine yet, and no project has booted the game.

item.title: AnyPS5 developer suspended on X, with no evidence Sony or Rockstar was behind it
item.description: The suspension is real, but the cause isn't public, and an account blaming the two companies also promotes a crypto token.

item.title: XCL takes the lead after running its first retail Xbox games on PC
item.description: The Wine-style layer says Minecraft Preview is fully playable on Windows. GTA VI still can't start, because its executable is missing.

item.title: The missing GTA VI executable is due Monday at 18:00 CET, and votes cost money
item.description: Cyberleek's countdown ends at 17:00 UTC on Nov 23 while its site charges for poll votes; the early-release token goal is reportedly down to $6 million.

item.title: Re-uploads of the leading GTA VI projects are already circulating
item.description: On its first run, our scout found three copies of Leonida under other accounts. One had been renamed and given a vague description.

item.title: Cyberleek's Xbox build is out, except the file that runs it
item.description: The leaker says the missing executable will be released on Monday, Nov 23, or sooner if its meme coin reaches a $15 million market cap.

item.title: Every “GTA VI for PC” download is fake, and some empty your accounts
item.description: Security firms have tracked tens of thousands of GTA VI malware detections, and a ready-made scam kit is for sale on the dark web.

item.title: Take-Two hits GTA V ports on GitHub, saying “bring your own files” is no defence
item.description: Four DMCA notices, filed the day before GTA VI launched, took down unofficial GTA V ports along with hundreds of forks.

item.title: The 2022 GTA VI hacker pleads guilty and will be sentenced on Monday
item.description: Arion Kurtaj admitted hacking Rockstar and posting about 90 development clips. His sentencing falls on the same day as Cyberleek's executable deadline.
